reconcile.note: Clarke distinguishes the patriarchs' sight of symbolic manifestations of God's presence from a literal vision of his invisible essence, which John denies anyone has had.

discrepancy.note: Remsburg juxtaposes Jacob's face-to-face vision of God against John's flat denial that anyone has ever seen him.

quotes.text: Is God a visible Being? Jacob: “I have seen God face to face” (Genesis xxxii, 30). John: “No man hath seen God at any time” (i, 18).
quotes.attr: John E. Remsburg (d. 1919), The Christ (1909), on Genesis 32:30 and John 1:18.

sides.snippet: They saw God, and ate and drank.
sides.verseText: He didn't lay his hand on the nobles of the children of Israel. They saw God, and ate and drank.

sides.snippet: You cannot see my face, for man may not see me and live.
sides.verseText: He said, \"You cannot see my face, for man may not see me and live.\"
